central_topic: Estimation error of regression-based global average treatment effect (GATE) estimators under network interference, characterized as exposure-mapping misspecification and corner-exposure extrapolation bias versus variance, with undercovering confidence intervals.
core_methods: regression-based GATE estimation with a fitted exposure mapping and BIC-gated library
HC1 sandwich confidence intervals widened by estimator spread
comparators: Horvitz-Thompson / Hajek estimators under exposure mappings
result_driven_themes: accuracy governed by fidelity of the fitted exposure mapping to the generating mechanism
interval undercoverage (0.839 vs nominal 0.95) from ignored cluster dependence

queries.query: causal inference under misspecified exposure mapping network interference
queries.rationale: Targets 'thesis-exposure-mapping-misspecification' (introduction, anchor: 'accuracy is governed by the fidelity of the fitted exposure mapping to the generating mechanism'). Only Aronow2013EstimatingAC is cited for exposure mappings; the paper needs prior work on what happens when the mapping is wrong, to position its central thesis.

queries.query: average treatment effects under unknown interference structure
queries.rationale: Same target as above; covers unknown or arbitrary interference, which the thesis implies but the bibliography does not cite. Bhattacharya2019Uncertainty (network uncertainty) is already present, so this search is aimed at unknown-interference estimand and bias results instead.

queries.query: causal inference with interference spillover effects difference-in-means bias randomized experiments
queries.rationale: Targets 'intro-interference-dim-bias' (introduction, anchor: 'The difference-in-means (DiM) estimator, which is unbiased without interference, is systematically biased for the GATE under interference'). The opening claims about no-interference violations and DiM bias have no foundational citation; only HT estimators are cited there.

queries.query: variance estimation and confidence intervals under network dependence in interference experiments
queries.rationale: Targets 'reliability-interval-undercoverage' (results, reliability subsection, anchor: 'ignores cluster dependence under the cluster design and uses no resampling'). The 0.839 vs 0.95 coverage result is explained by HC1 intervals ignoring dependence, but no work on network-dependent variance estimation or HAC/cluster-robust inference is cited beyond Han2023ModelbasedRA.

forbidden_query_patterns: generic optimization / benchmarking / scientific method / AI scientist phrasing
campaign order, iteration, milestone or search-history phrasing
graph neural network / spectral convolution queries
queries for topics already well covered: HT estimators, graph cluster randomization, GATE regression adjustment, staggered rollout, covariance-optimized designs
any query targeting the specific published paper on this research question, its title, authors, or results
internal harness terms (combined_score, rubric, eligible, worker)
